one_liner: Entry-to-mid-level administrative support role at ICE handling budget, procurement, HR, property, space, travel, vendors, and fleet management for an office, with promotion potential to GS-12.
fit_summary: This Direct Hire, public announcement has no clearance requirement, and Arlington is commutable from Manassas, so Daniel can realistically compete. His IEM work maps to the GS-7 or GS-9 specialized experience (applying procedures, working with varied contacts, verifying facts, ensuring compliance), and he did hands-on administrative operations there: purchasing and tracking supplies, vendor relationships, spending reports, office security, travel support and help with onboarding. GS-9 is the level to aim for.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) under OPM Direct Hire Authority; veterans' preference and category rating do not apply, and no federal status is needed.
GS-07 requires one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-05 showing at least 3 of the 4 listed duties, or one full year of graduate education, or a combination.

GS-09 requires one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-07 showing at least 3 of the 6 listed duties (e.g., reconciling discrepancies, ensuring compliance), or a master's degree or 2 years of graduate study, or a combination.
No clearance is required, but a pre-employment drug test and background checks apply; qualifications must be met by the closing date of 2026-11-06.
Positions are located in Arlington, VA; Irving, TX; or Washington, DC, with no telework or remote option.
keywords: ensuring compliance with applicable regulations and procedures
verifying and assessing relevant facts from several sources
strategy: Apply on opening day (2026-10-30), because the first 150 applicants receive first consideration and the window is only one week.

Frame your IEM role around what you actually did, such as tracking deliverables, reconciling data or invoices, applying FEMA or program guidance, coordinating with government clients and vendors, and supporting reports, and then mirror the specialized-experience duty language in your own words without copy-pasting.
Write the IEM entry so at least three GS-9 duties are clearly visible as separate bullets, and include start and end dates (month/year) and hours per week to establish one full year.
Keep the resume to two pages, put IEM first with the most detail, and condense older or unrelated roles to a line or two.
Upload his George Mason transcript: a master's can meet GS-9 on education where the posting allows it.
Answer the questionnaire honestly and choose an expert level only where a resume bullet backs it up, then set aside quiet time for the online competency assessment.
resume_bullets: Handled office manager duties at IEM (2019–2024): office security, first-line IT troubleshooting, deliveries and conference supplies, and help with onboarding and offboarding.
Answered employee travel-expense questions in Certify and booked flights for corporate-level staff.
Procured and tracked medical supplies for sites in six states, and set up relationships with medical supply and truck rental vendors (2021–2022).
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you found an inconsistency in data or records. How did you resolve it?
How would you handle a vendor or internal office that was not meeting expectations on a service your office depends on?
Describe how you prioritize competing administrative requests from multiple managers under deadline pressure.
Give an example of applying a regulation or procedure to a situation where the guidance was not perfectly clear.
watch_outs: The application window is only one week and consideration is capped at the first 150 applicants, so apply early.
The posting has no telework option, and the Manassas-to-Arlington commute is daily.
The duties are administrative and operational (fleet, property, procurement) rather than policy or public-facing work, so make sure this fits your career goals.
The Major Duties text describes the GS-12 level, so expect starting work at GS-7 or GS-9 to be more limited.
